Egalitarianism

/ih-gal-uh-TAIR-ee-uh-niz-uhm/ - the stress falls on TAIR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Egalitarianism means the belief that all people deserve equal rights and opportunities.

The kitchen's egalitarianism was total: head chef and newest dishwasher ate the same staff meal at the same long table.

Worked Example

Ships' articles from the 1720s reveal a rough egalitarianism among pirate crews: every hand voted on the destination, plunder was split by published shares, and a captain who lost the crew's confidence could be voted right back out of his cabin.

Egalitarianism is the principle, not the mood: a belief that equal rights and opportunities belong to everyone. Generosity hands things down; egalitarianism refuses the ladder altogether, insisting no one stands above anyone to begin with.

How Egalitarianism Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

equality

equality: the condition itself; egalitarianism is the belief that the condition should hold

fairness

fairness: even-handed treatment case by case, without the sweeping creed

Antonyms

elitism

elitism: the belief that a select few deserve more say

hierarchy

hierarchy: an arrangement of ranks stacked above one another

How Strong Is It? — impartiality → egalitarianism → leveling

impartiality vs. egalitarianism

impartiality vs. egalitarianism: Impartiality is the milder ask — one referee favoring neither side today; egalitarianism claims equal standing for everyone, everywhere.

leveling vs. egalitarianism

leveling vs. egalitarianism: Leveling goes further than egalitarianism: equal rights and chances no longer satisfy it — every difference of wealth and rank must be flattened too.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — egal

Root — egal: equal (French égal, from Latin aequus, level)

Suffix — -itarian

Suffix — -itarian: believing in, advocating

Suffix — -ism

Suffix — -ism: belief, system

Put it together

Put it together: Egal- (equal — French égal, from Latin aequus, 'level') + -itarian (believing in) + -ism (belief, system) = the belief in equal standing. French revolutionaries shouted égalité; English borrowed the root and stacked two suffixes onto it to name the conviction itself.

Use the root in a new word: equator

Use the root in a new word: equator: Crossing the equator, the crew held the ship's traditional line-crossing ceremony.

Word Choice

formal / academic

Egalitarianism names the belief — the conviction that equal rights and opportunities belong to everyone. For the condition itself, say equality; for the adjective, egalitarian (in this unit's reference list). It is about standing, not kindness: a charity can be generous and still not egalitarian.
